Bethzur
bĕth-zûr´
n. (a hill town of Judah; fortified by Rehoboam and rebuilt after the exile)
Hebrew beyth tsur, house of rock — a name from the ridge it stood on, south of Jerusalem on the road to Hebron.

Biblical Definition

Bethzur appears in Judah's hill-country allotment: “Halhul, Bethzur, and Gedor” (Josh 15:58), and in the genealogy of Caleb's line: “Maon was the father of Bethzur” (1Ch 2:45). Rehoboam made it one of his defended cities: “And Bethzur, and Shoco, and Adullam” (2Ch 11:7). And after the exile its ruler took a share of the wall: “After him repaired Nehemiah the son of Azbuk, the ruler of the half part of Bethzur, unto the place over against the sepulchres of David” (Neh 3:16), the Levites repairing next to him (Neh 3:17).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines a rock as a large mass of stony matter, and figuratively defense, means of safety, protection, strength.

expand to see more

ROCK, n. A large mass of stony matter, usually compounded of two or more simple minerals.

ROCK, n. In Scripture, defense; means of safety; protection; strength; asylum.

REPAIR, v.t. To restore to a sound or good state after decay, injury or partial destruction.

Key Scripture

Josh 15:58 — "Halhul, Bethzur, and Gedor,"

1Ch 2:45 — "And the son of Shammai was Maon: and Maon was the father of Bethzur."

2Ch 11:7 — "And Bethzur, and Shoco, and Adullam,"

Neh 3:16 — "After him repaired Nehemiah the son of Azbuk, the ruler of the half part of Bethzur, unto the place over against the sepulchres of David, and to the pool that was made, and unto the house of the mighty."

Modern Corruption

Nehemiah 3 is a list of names against sections of wall, and the Holy Spirit thought the assignment of ordinary men worth recording.

expand to see more

Nehemiah 3 is one of the least quoted and most encouraging chapters in the Old Testament. It is a register: the high priest and his brethren built the sheep gate; the men of Jericho built next to them; the goldsmiths, the apothecaries, the merchants, the Levites, the rulers of half-districts like Bethzur, each with a named length of wall. Some are noted for building over against their own house. One family is noted for refusing — the nobles of Tekoa put not their necks to the work of their Lord. The wall went up in fifty-two days because a hundred small assignments were kept, and the record of who kept them is Scripture.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that God keeps the register. First Corinthians 3:8 says every man shall receive his own reward according to his own labour; Hebrews 6:10 says God is not unrighteous to forget your work and labour of love; Malachi 3:16 describes a book of remembrance written before Him for them that feared the LORD. The ruler of half Bethzur repaired a stretch of wall by the sepulchres of David and is named for it two and a half thousand years later. Faithfulness in a small assigned section is the ordinary shape of Christian service, and it is not anonymous.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew tsur (H6697), rock, cliff, and figuratively God as refuge; chazaq (H2388), to repair, strengthen; pelek (H6418), district, part.

expand to see more

Hebrew tsur (H6697) — rock, strength, refuge; Joshua 15:58, Deuteronomy 32:4, Psalm 18:2.

Hebrew chazaq (H2388) — to repair, make strong; Nehemiah 3:16, 3:17.

Hebrew pelek (H6418) — district, part, portion; Nehemiah 3:16, 3:12.

Hebrew qeber (H6913) — grave, sepulchre; Nehemiah 3:16, Genesis 23:6.

Hebrew metsurah (H4694) — fortification, stronghold; 2 Chronicles 11:5, 11:10.

Usage

"“Halhul, Bethzur, and Gedor” — the hill country of Judah."

"“And Bethzur, and Shoco, and Adullam” — Rehoboam's defended cities."

"“The ruler of the half part of Bethzur” — named for his stretch of wall."
